title: Debugging debugging information using dynamic call trees
Anchor, Tensor, and Skin: A Fixed-Domain Decomposition Theorem for Admissible Description (Normal Form Capstone)
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: This paper establishes a canonical decomposition for admissible description within a fixed domain. A determinate description must preserve three distinct kinds of work: the conditions that fix the original problem; the content that determines the required answers; the realization that carries or presents that content. These roles are named anchor, tensor, and skin. The terms describe functional roles in an admissible construction. “Tensor” does not presuppose vector-space structure, multilinearity, or a tensor-product operation. The central result is a choice-free dependent reconstruction: D → T → K where: K records the interpreted anchor context; T records the complete original-answer profile within that context; the realization fibres retain the descriptions that carry each context-content pair. The decomposition preserves the actual dependency between context, content, and realization. It does not assume that these layers vary independently or form a Cartesian product. Canonical Reconstruction and Uniqueness For an independently interpreted descriptive carrier, the paper constructs a tower of surjections from descriptions to complete content and then to anchor context. The canonical reconstruction theorem proves that: every original description is recovered from its anchor, complete content, and realization-fibre membership; the reconstruction requires no arbitrary choice of representatives; the middle content space is the minimal complete interface for the declared original uses; any two minimal complete presentations are related by a unique commuting bijection; faithful minimal reconstruction systems have the same dependent fibre structure. This separates several conclusions that are often conflated: a unique complete content representation; a unique realization decomposition over that content; a unique representative; a unique physical or mathematical occupant. The theorem establishes the first two at their proper levels. It does not select an arbitrary representative from every realization fibre or imply that the fibres are singletons. Anchor, Tensor, and Skin Effects The paper classifies every specified interpreted variation according to the first level at which it changes the canonical tower: Anchor effect: the interpreted context changes. Tensor effect: the context is fixed, but the complete original-answer profile changes. Skin effect: context and complete content are preserved, while the realization changes. These three effects are mutually exclusive and exhaustive for the stated variation family. A skin variation preserves every required original answer, including semantic definedness. A tensor variation may contain many independent coordinates and does not reduce content to one scalar quantity. An anchor variation may also alter numerical answers, but those answers belong to a changed context rather than constituting a second effect within the original fixed context. Canonical Role Refinement Raw components need not be pure. A single symbol, clause, field, or component may exhibit different effects under different permitted variations. The paper therefore constructs the unique coarsest homogeneous refinement: each refined component class has one realized effect type; mixed raw components split into their actual anchor, tensor, and skin incidence classes; every adequate effect classifier factors uniquely through the minimal role classifier; the number of minimal classifier states equals the number of realized effect types; exactly three states are required only when all three effects are actually realized. This is a theorem about interpreted variation incidences, not a claim that every written object contains three independently stored fields. Functional Minimality and Deletion A required function survives deletion or recoding exactly when it factors through the retained code. If a proposed reduction merges two descriptions that have different required original outcomes, no procedure using only the retained code can recover both outcomes. The collision is an explicit witness of lost admissible work. Conversely, if the required profile factors through the retained interface, the original function remains represented even if its former field name or storage location disappears. The paper distinguishes: deletion of representational surplus; preservation of complete original content; recovery of the original description; coverage of every required realization fibre. An exact content interface may discard skin while failing to reconstruct the original descriptive carrier. That is not a contradiction: semantic preservation and description recovery are different tasks. Independent Factorization and Compatibility The canonical decomposition is generally dependent. Content may depend on anchor context, and realization fibres may depend on both context and content. A Cartesian product decomposition requires additional conditions: injectivity of the proposed coordinate map; equality between its image and the declared compatible domain; compatible identifications of context, content, and realization fibres; rectangularity if every individually available coordinate combination is claimed to be realizable. The paper proves that independent recombination is not implied by individual availability. Joint compatibility must be checked explicitly. A collection of individually admissible components may fail to form an admissible tuple because a relational condition is not retained by the proposed interfaces. Skin Transformations and Operator Identity All content-preserving realization maps are characterized as fibrewise maps within the realization fibres. Their invertible instances are exactly the fibrewise bijections. A normalization or representative-selection map may preserve complete content without preserving the identity of the original representative. It is therefore not automatically an identity-preserving reconstruction of the original description. For operators, the paper constructs an inspectable semantic envelope containing the original: metadata; domain and applicability; licence and check outcomes; conditional results; retained state and output profiles. Under explicit primitive adequacy and joint-domain conditions, equality of these envelopes is equivalent to equality under every declared finite use. The result extends through sequential composition, strict binding, finite products, conditionals, and typed joint constructors. This establishes operator identity relative to a declared finite-use language. It does not identify different mechanisms merely because they share a scalar output, nor does an envelope named “complete” establish its own coverage. Scope and Nonclaims The theorem is relative to a fixed original descriptive problem, declared use family, and admissibility-preserving comparison class. It does not claim: that three independently stored fields are always necessary; that anchor, tensor, and skin form an unrestricted Cartesian product; that every raw component has one pure role; that every realization fibre has a canonical representative; that a complete content quotient identifies the original occurrence; that mathematical compatibility implies physical execution; that operator-envelope equality identifies equal mechanisms; that the entire reference edition has been newly formalized in Lean. The AASC kernel governs every determinate description, record, carrier, operator, and endpoint by necessity. The present paper concerns how their particular admissible descriptions preserve context, content, realization, and operator use within a fixed domain. Role in the AASC Programme This paper supplies the decomposition layer of the AASC foundation: kernel necessity → fixed-domain content → anchor/tensor/skin factorization → faithful reconstruction → compositional operator identity. Its central result is that admissible description has a canonical role structure, but not an arbitrary field layout. Required work survives lawful encoding; representational surplus may be removed; mixed components admit canonical role refinement; and every claim of independence, recombination, or operator identity is governed by an explicit reconstruction or compatibility theorem. Keywords AASC; Anchor-Tensor-Skin decomposition; fixed-domain admissibility; admissible description; canonical reconstruction; role factorization; anchor context; tensor content; representational skin; minimal complete interface; faithful redescription; functional minimality; joint compatibility; operator identity; realization fibres

title: A Fixed-Domain Exhaustion Theorem Standing, Consequence, and Compositional Closure under Typed Boundary Discipline
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: This paper establishes a fixed-domain exhaustion theorem for standing-bearing construction under typed boundary discipline. The original bearer, questions, consequence relations, continuation obligations, and certificate conditions are specified independently of any proposed realization. A proposed representation is then assessed against those original requirements. It either preserves them or exhibits a concrete semantic defect. The central result is that every claimed complete realization has an exhaustive set of failure witnesses: an incorrect or omitted original result; a collision of indistinguishable inputs with different required outcomes; an unsafe continuation or omitted safe region; a failed premise, inference, license, or interpretation condition in an offered certificate. These alternatives are evaluated over interpreted proposals. Correctness is not assumed as an entrance condition, and a proposal cannot evade a witnessed failure through relabeling, postprocessing, or a new authority label. Complete Interfaces and Canonical Quotients The paper first constructs the complete outcome profile of the original task. This profile records every required result, including application-definedness and continuation behavior where relevant. From it, the paper proves: existence of a canonical minimal complete quotient; unique factorization of every adequate representation through that quotient; a separating original question for every distinct quotient class; an exact fibre criterion for lossless representation; the precise condition under which the complete interface reduces to a single qualification bit. A binary interface is therefore not assumed. It is valid only when every required outcome is constant on the fibres of the qualification bit. Equal qualification alone does not justify identifying objects with different required uses, continuation behavior, or original identity. The paper distinguishes: one original consequence; the complete descriptive interface; a family of candidate occupants; a unique occupant; a unique decomposition. Each requires a different proof obligation. Uniqueness of one original consequence does not imply a singleton family of occupants, and a unique admissible set does not imply a unique element within that set. Typed Compositional Closure A central contribution is the exact compositional closure theorem for typed finite constructions. Primitive partial operations and observations are treated with their domains, output classes, and definedness conditions preserved explicitly. The paper proves that a proposed quotient or reduced interface supports compositional reuse precisely when: primitive operation domains are saturated on its fibres; defined outputs descend to the same retained output classes; primitive observations preserve both definedness and value; joint constructor domains are saturated on retained input tuples; jointly constructed outputs agree on equal retained data. These local conditions extend by induction to: all finite operation words; finite observation grammars; strict constructor trees; many-sorted finite assemblies; joint compatibility relations; generated continuation profiles. A mismatch in any generated expression has a finite witness at a primitive operation, observation, joint domain, or constructor output. The proof therefore distinguishes observation completeness from update descent: an interface may preserve every displayed observation while still failing to support the operations that later uses require. Fixed-Domain Exhaustion The fixed-domain exhaustion theorem compares every proposed realization with an independently specified original task. For any interpreted proposal claiming complete answers, a complete interface, a robust interior, or certificate support, one of the following holds: all original semantic obligations are satisfied; or the proposal has an original-result defect, information defect, continuation defect, or support defect. The theorem covers: surplus asserted records; omitted required results; failed absence claims; indistinguishable inputs requiring different outcomes; unsafe admitted configurations; omitted sound configurations; false premises; invalid inferences; failed interpretation or transfer conditions. The witness classes may overlap. They are a proof organization for the complete original task, not a claim that every failure in reality belongs to one of four disjoint categories. A faithful redescription, quotient re-encoding, or new authority label cannot: make an incorrect original result correct; restore a missing required result without supplying it; recover a discarded distinction from unchanged input; make an unsafe continuation safe; validate an unsupported certificate. A correction, new justified observation, or independently sound construction may discharge the failed obligation. That is an actual change in warrant or construction, not a presentational escape from the theorem. History, Irreversible Retention, and Grounded Authorization The paper separately establishes conservation for original consequences and retained historical claims. A later successful construction does not replace an earlier failed occurrence. A corrected report may improve knowledge of the original event without altering its original conditions. Historical retention is also distinguished from endpoint absorption: a positive endpoint certifies the entire retained path only when the transition system satisfies the relevant negative-absorption condition. Grounded authorization is treated through least closure from independently warranted premises. Composition of sound warrants preserves authorization, but a cycle of mutually assumed warrants cannot supply its own first ground. This prevents unsupported authority from entering through increasingly elaborate certificate structure. Consequence Determination and Downstream Use The paper gives exact criteria for exporting its results to later mathematical and physical constructions. A downstream application must independently specify: the bearer and original question; the original result or consequence relation; the intended observations and continuation family; the interpretation of its typed operations and constructors; the coverage relation between its formal language and the original task; any additional existence, occupancy, or uniqueness conditions. The exhaustion theorem constrains same-task claims. It does not derive a new physical law, numerical value, populated realization, or unique occupant from the exhaustion taxonomy alone. Scope The result is a structural theorem over a fixed comparison class and an independently specified determinate-use problem. It is not: an enumeration of every possible formal or physical system; a universal algorithm for deciding semantic correctness; a claim that every admissible interior is nonempty; a claim that a greatest interior is a singleton; a replacement for domain-specific realization or existence proofs; a proof that eventual success, fairness, termination, or controllability follows from finite safety; a completed proof-assistant formalization of the entire manuscript. The governing scope is fixed-domain and same-task. A changed bearer, question, repertoire, or consequence relation requires its own theorem or a justified transfer result. Role in the AASC Programme This paper supplies the exhaustion and composition layer of the AASC foundation: kernel necessity → complete interface → typed compositional closure → witnessed exhaustion → consequence determination. Its contribution is to make closure inspectable. A same-scope construction remains admissible only when its original results, retained distinctions, operation domains, joint compatibilities, historical conditions, and certificate warrants all survive the declared boundary discipline. Exhaustion is established as a theorem over admissibility-bearing variation within the fixed comparison class, not as an enumeration of cases. Keywords AASC; fixed-domain exhaustion; admissibility; standing; typed boundary discipline; canonical quotient; semantic coverage; compositional closure; complete interface; faithful redescription; consequence determination; greatest safe interior; irreversible retention; grounded authorization; same-scope closure

title: Canadian Parliament Open Data and Embedded Vector Knowledge Base: InsightToast (UIST '26) Supplemental Dataset
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Canadian Parliament Open Data and Embedded Vector Knowledge Base: InsightToast (UIST '26) Supplemental Dataset 📄 Paper: https://doi.org/10.1145/3830398.3830522💻 Code: https://github.com/ubixgroup/InsightToast Supplemental dataset for the paper: InsightToast: Proactive Information Retrieval & Glanceable Visualization in the Side Channel of Data-Rich Meetings Mohammad Abolnejadian and Matthew Brehmer. Proceedings of the 39th Annual ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology (UIST '26). DOI: 10.1145/3830398.3830522 This dataset provides a collection of 43,878 open legislative records from the Canadian House of Commons, spanning 1994 to 2025, covering document types such as debates (Hansard), legislative bills, committee reports, petitions, recorded votes, order papers, and Library of Parliament research publications. It is released at three stages of the same pipeline: the raw collected documents, a processed corpus that has been passed through an ETL pipeline and chunked for use in a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline, and an embedded, pre-indexed vector store built from that processed corpus. The dataset supports the development and user study of the InsightToast project. The embedded form can be placed directly into the project's codebase, open sourced at https://github.com/ubixgroup/InsightToast, where it serves as the knowledge base when InsightToast operates as a proactive side-channel assistant in policy discussion meetings. Usage in the InsightToast Backend Only qdrant_storage.tar.gz is required to run the backend. Extract it into the root of the InsightToast project, so that qdrant_storage/ sits alongside docker-compose.yml, and start the services: tar -xzf qdrant_storage.tar.gz -C /path/to/InsightToast/ cd /path/to/InsightToast docker compose up --build -d Contents File What it is Approx. size parliament_data.tar.gz Raw source corpus of 43,878 parliamentary records, as 57,124 files (.txt + .pdf) 8.1 GB compressed / 11 GB extracted parliament_data_processed.tar.gz Processed corpus: the same records cleaned, normalized, and chunked into RAG-ready JSON 2.1 GB compressed / 9.1 GB extracted qdrant_storage.tar.gz Pre-indexed Qdrant vector store, ready to mount as the knowledge base 21 GB compressed / 27 GB extracted parliament_data.STRUCTURE.txt Manifest of the raw corpus, viewable without downloading the archive small parliament_data_processed.STRUCTURE.txt Manifest of the processed corpus small qdrant_storage.STRUCTURE.txt Manifest of the vector store small SHA256SUMS.txt SHA-256 checksums for the three archives small Verify the archives after download: sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS.txt Source Corpus: Raw Parliamentary Documents parliament_data.tar.gz contains open legislative documents collected across the range of record types produced by the Canadian House of Commons and the Library of Parliament, including the proceedings of debate, the texts of bills as tabled, the reports of standing committees, the petitions presented to the House, and the recorded outcomes of divisions. The documents were assembled from three public sources: the House of Commons (ourcommons.ca, including the Legislative Information service, LEGISinfo), the Library of Parliament of Canada (parl-gc.primo.exlibrisgroup.com), and the independent open-data mirror openparliament.ca. No private, personal, or access-restricted material is included; Member of Parliament profiles contain only information published in an official public capacity. Total: 43,878 parliamentary records, distributed across 57,124 files (43,634 .txt + 13,490 .pdf). Each record is provided as extracted plain text, with the source PDF alongside it under the same basename where one exists, so records that carry both formats account for two files. Temporal coverage: documents span the 35th through 45th Parliaments. Debates run from 1994-01-17 to 2025-10-10; coverage of the other record types varies by type. Languages: the source records are bilingual (English and French), as published by Parliament. Filename conventions: debates use sitting dates (YYYY-MM-DD- .txt); bills, journals, order papers, and votes use - - (for example, 37-1-C-10); petitions and Library of Parliament publications use slugified titles. Category Files Description debates/ 18,347 House of Commons debates (Hansard transcripts), one file per sitting day bills/ 10,561 Legislative bills, full text plus the original tabled PDF journals/ 7,038 Official Journals of the House (daily record of decisions) petitions/ 6,093 e-Petitions and paper petitions presented to the House votes/ 4,521 Recorded division and vote results order-papers/ 4,228 Order Paper and Notice Paper (daily agenda) library/ 2,202 Library of Parliament publications and tabled agreements committee-reports/ 1,577 Standing and joint committee reports, grouped into 27 committee subfolders politicians/ 1,319 Member of Parliament profiles research/ 1,210 Library of Parliament research and HillNotes publications committees/ 28 Committee mandate and description summaries Total 57,124 See parliament_data.STRUCTURE.txt for the full breakdown, including all committee subfolders. Processed Corpus: Cleaned and Chunked Records parliament_data_processed.tar.gz contains the same corpus after the ETL pipeline that turns each document into retrievable units. Documents are parsed from their metadata header and routed by document_type. Bilingual records are language-identified with langdetect and reduced to their English content by an LLM pass. PDFs are structurally partitioned with unstructured's partition_pdf into text, table, and image elements; table elements are linearized into prose by an LLM, and salient figures are captioned, written to images/, and linked from their chunk via has_images. Records whose content is inherently tabular, namely recorded votes, petitions, and Member profiles, are rendered into natural-language narratives to keep them semantically retrievable rather than reducing to fields. Type-specific pre-segmentation then splits debates on speaker turns, preserving the speaker, section, and timestamp, before every stream passes through a RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter (1,000 characters, 200 overlap); each resulting chunk is tagged with its content_type (text, table, or image) and its provenance. The output is one JSON document per record, holding the record's metadata and its ordered list of chunks: { "metadata": { "document_type": "debate", "session": "35-1", "date": "1994-01-17", "language": "en", "source_file": "debates/1994-01-17-1.txt", "source_url": "...", "total_chunks": 51 }, "chunks": [ { "chunk_id": 0, "content": "...", "metadata": { "speaker": "...", "section": "...", "content_type": "text", "has_images": false } } ] } Volume: 42,014 JSON records and 2,170 extracted images, totaling 6,379,732 chunks, which is the set embedded into the knowledge base below. Traceability: every record's metadata.source_file links back to its file in the raw corpus. Coverage: most record types are processed in full; committee-report and library are present as subsets of the raw corpus. See parliament_data_processed.STRUCTURE.txt for per-category counts. Indexed Knowledge Base qdrant_storage.tar.gz contains the processed corpus above embedded and indexed into Qdrant, ready to serve as the retrieval backend with no further processing. Collection Size Vectors Role parliament_documents ~27 GB 768-dim, cosine Primary knowledge base retrieved during meetings vega_altair_docs ~137 MB 768-dim, cosine Vega-Altair documentation used by the visualization-generator agent Embedding model: embeddinggemma:latest (served via Ollama), 768 dimensions, cosine distance. Qdrant version: built with qdrant/qdrant:v1.13.6. Qdrant's on-disk format is version-specific, so load this snapshot with the same or a compatible version to avoid migration issues. Inspecting the knowledge base on its own To browse or query the collections independently of the InsightToast stack, mount the extracted directory into a standalone Qdrant container: tar -xzf qdrant_storage.tar.gz # -> ./qdrant_storage/ docker run -p 6333:6333 \ -v "$(pwd)/qdrant_storage:/qdrant/storage" \ qdrant/qdrant:v1.13.6 # reports the collection and its point count: curl http://localhost:6333/collections/parliament_documents License The parliamentary source documents and the embeddings derived from them are released under the Open Government Licence – Canada (https://open.canada.ca/en/open-government-licence-canada). When reusing them, include the attribution: Contains information licensed under the Open Government Licence – Canada. The original contributions in this record, namely the curation and compilation of the corpus, the ingestion and indexing pipeline output, and the accompanying documentation, are released under CC-BY 4.0. Note on parliamentary materials: reproductions of House of Commons proceedings, such as Hansard debates, are strictly governed by the House of Commons' own terms for the reproduction of parliamentary work rather than by a Government of Canada open-data licence. This dataset is redistributed for non-commercial academic research use, faithfully and without alteration of meaning. Reuse beyond research should be checked against the applicable House of Commons reproduction terms. title: WHERE DOES THE DARK HORSE WIN? The Formal Best Theories of The Philosophy of Virtues Research Programme, Their Strengths Compared with Those of the Leading Classical and Contemporary Philosophers, Assessed Across Twenty-Eight Domains, and the Boundary Where Its Advantage Ends.
abstract: “The Dark Horse wins in ten domains of twenty-eight. Finishes in the top places in fourteen domains, and does not take part in the race in the four remaining categories. It’s not bad at all. Place your bets.” Highlights The programme is strongest exactly where its primitive does work no other primitive does — the structure of virtue, the mechanism of corruption, the prediction of capture, the ontology of collective moral properties, and the governance of artificial systems. It weakens in proportion to its distance from that centre, even though the originalities are numerous. The pattern is not a defect. It is what a real advantage looks like when it is measured rather than asserted. The Verdict at a Glance Twenty-eight domains, each assessed against a named rival on criteria fixed in advance. The full map, with the specific advantage and the formal object that carries it in each case, is §2. Tier Verdict Domains A Advantage strongly defensible Structure of virtue · Corruption and vice · Institutional capture · Collective virtue · AI governance · AI sycophancy · Machine virtue · Research practice · Forgery and authenticity · The measurement of character B Genuine contribution, close antecedent, priority shared Aesthetics · Truth · The three transcendentals · Economics · Love · Philosophy of mind · Political philosophy · Transgression · Formation under suppression · Martyrdom and persistence · Immortality · Institutions and civilisational forgery · Crypto-religion and syncretism · Evolution and signalling C Claim not sustainable as stated Origin of life · Quantum measurement · Cosmology · Theology Abstract A theory that claims to win everywhere has told you nothing about where it wins. This paper asks the sharper question — in which domains, against which named rival, for which specific reason — and answers it across the whole corpus of the Philosophy of Virtues: twenty-eight domains, from the structure of virtue to the evolution of species. The verdict is a distribution, and the distribution is the result. In ten domains the programme’s advantage is strongly defensible, and in three of those it is close to unopposed. Its claims there are not merely novel but specific: the Inversion Theorem predicts that a corrupted institution decouples procedural integrity from output orientation, where privation theory predicts the two decline together; the Capture Law predicts which of three corruption channels opens, from two dispositional properties of the activity, where Goodhart’s Law has one channel and reaches only gaming; the Collective Inversion Theorem predicts that a city can invert while every inhabitant remains free and uncoerced, and that above a threshold of observability, communities with identical inputs separate into stable branches with a discontinuous jump in conditional variance — a claim about second moments where the standing sociology predicts a shift in means. Two further domains entered at this tier with the forgery cluster: the Competence Theorem predicts that damage rises with the fidelity of a fake, where the aesthetics of forgery predicts that skill mitigates; and the three-channel measurement failure is derived from forgeability, where the psychometric and situationist traditions argue over instruments without asking whether character can be read from a form at all. These are the claims of a theory built to be wrong in identifiable ways, which is the only kind that can be right in interesting ones. In fourteen domains the contribution is genuine and the priority is not. Two findings, established here, require correction across the corpus. Schiller, in the Kallias letters of 1793, defined beauty as Freiheit in der Erscheinung — freedom in appearance — with self-determination, “the being-determined-through-itself of the thing,” as his criterion; this is the thesis of the programme’s aesthetics, stated 233 years earlier. And “operational closure” is Francisco Varela’s own term, in a field where organisational closure is not a challenger to the standing view of life’s origin but the family that standing view belongs to, running from Rosen’s (M,R)-systems through autopoiesis, Kauffman’s autocatalytic sets, Gánti’s chemoton, and the closure of constraints. In both cases the defensible claim is first derivation, not first statement — and in the aesthetic case the theory of the occupied form, which Schiller entirely lacks, remains the programme’s own. In four domains the claim does not hold and is withdrawn or re-scoped here: origin of life, quantum measurement, cosmology, and the theological identity thesis. The apparatus was built from an ethical primitive and is not equipped to displace mature sciences under heavy observational constraint. The dark horse wins where its primitive does work no other primitive does, and its advantage thins in exact proportion to its distance from that centre. Keywords: virtue theory; freedom; inversion; institutional capture; transcendentals; research programme appraisal; priority; evolution of species; Philosophy of Virtues, Alguilas-AI
